title: Arcads Pricing: Credits, Trial and Alternatives
summary: Understand Arcads pricing through verified credit rules, trial terms and a cost worksheet. Compare self-serve alternatives with managed video ad production.
body_markdown:
## Which Arcads alternatives should you compare?


Choose the alternative around the work you want to do yourself. A URL-based workflow, an avatar editor and a production team are different routes to an ad. This shortlist identifies a task to evaluate rather than declaring a universal quality winner.


Option Verified workflow Consider it when Boundary to evaluate


[Creatify](https://creatify.ai/features/url-to-video) Turns a product URL into video-ad creative Your approved product page is the starting asset Review the extracted claims, assets and generated script yourself


[MakeUGC](https://makeugc.ai/) AI video and image creation You want another self-serve production workflow to compare Run the same script and product task before judging output


[HeyGen](https://www.heygen.com/pricing) Avatar video plans, with translation and voice features Presenter or localization work is central Check the credit cost and export features of the selected plan


Knowlify[Meta ads service](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency) Creative production and Meta campaign management, or creative-only delivery You want a team to make ads and optionally own Meta campaigns Agree formats, approvals, campaign responsibilities and a private quote; media spend separate


For two self-serve candidates, our[Creatify versus Arcads comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/creatify-vs-arcads) adds product-specific context. Compare commercial rights and the steps left with your team as well as software access. Paying for a tool does not assign an editor or creative owner to your project.


## How should you plan a batch around a credit allowance?


Start with a production map rather than dividing credits by a headline video count. Write down the number of scripts, actors, generated takes, editing actions and final exports you expect to need. Mark which actions have a documented charge and which still need confirmation. The goal is to make your assumptions inspectable before paying, not to forecast a perfect acceptance rate.


For an illustrative batch, suppose the creative plan has two messages and two presenter treatments per message. That is four planned executions. It is not necessarily four generated takes, because a take can fail the brief or require another attempt. It is also not four independent concepts: the batch still contains two messages. Keep those three counts separate in the worksheet.


Use the documented 880-credit actor-and-caption example above only for tasks that meet its assumptions. Four such sequences would use 3,520 credits before retries or any other actions. This is arithmetic from the published schedule, not an Arcads package or a promise that the four outputs will be usable. If the real task includes a different model, more actors or additional processing, replace the calculation before committing the batch.


Reserve part of your intended allowance for correction work based on what your own pilot reveals. Do not borrow an assumed failure percentage from an unrelated team. After the pilot, classify the extra attempts: script change, performance preference, inaccurate product, technical failure or new concept. Some indicate a production problem to solve; others reflect a deliberate expansion of the brief.


## What is a useful evaluation within the trial window?


Prepare before activating a time-limited trial. Have one approved script, pronunciation notes, source assets and a written definition of an acceptable export. Choose a task that matters to your next campaign. A generic greeting can show that an avatar speaks, but it does not answer whether the workflow handles your product name, required demonstration or editing handoff.


Your first pass should establish the basic route from input to export. Record the settings and actual credits deducted. Then inspect the file against the brief before spending more of the allowance. If the output is unsuitable, change one identifiable input when practical and explain what the next attempt should resolve. Repeatedly generating without recording the reason produces a weaker buying decision.


Do not try to test every advertised capability within a small allowance. Select the one or two jobs that would justify the subscription. A team buying for presenter ads might prioritize delivery and handoff to an editor; a product-animation team has a different requirement. If the trial allowance cannot support a representative task, record that limitation and request a relevant demonstration or clarify paid evaluation terms.


At the end, write a short decision note: what was attempted, what was accepted, what remains untested, and what the next paid period would produce. Record the cancellation deadline separately so the commercial decision does not depend on remembering it while reviewing creative. Cancelling a trial and requesting a refund are distinct actions with different conditions.


## When does a larger plan solve the wrong problem?


A larger allowance addresses a shortage of capacity only when your existing process can turn that capacity into useful output. Review the rejection log first. If most unused work comes from changing scripts after rendering, agree the script earlier. If a specific product depiction never meets the brief, investigate a different production treatment before purchasing more attempts at the same treatment.


An uneven schedule also deserves a separate calculation. A team with occasional launches should model the periods it actually needs, including the documented rollover or reset rules for the selected tier. Buying enough credits for the busiest month can leave a different utilization pattern from buying for a steady weekly queue. Neither model is inherently correct; the contract and production calendar should fit each other.


For an in-house team, the right next purchase could be editing time, stronger product footage or a clearer approval process. For a team without an owner for finished ads, compare a managed proposal. Knowlify offers creative production with end-to-end Meta campaign management, or creative-only work when your buyer remains in place. Pricing is private and media spend is separate.


Use the same two-message batch for the comparison. Ask the service provider to identify what counts as a concept, how variants are approved and who owns campaign decisions. That gives you two useful decisions: which production workflow fits, and whether you also want to delegate Meta management. A software credit calculation answers only part of the first decision.


## When does managed production make sense?


Consider managed production when you can supply product truth and approve work but need another team to own the production queue. Keep software in-house when hands-on control is valuable and your team has a repeatable way to make accepted ads. Use the same brief and acceptance checklist for both paths.


Knowlify's[video ad production](https://knowlify.com/video-ad-production) and[creative subscription](https://knowlify.com/creative-as-a-service) cover concept-to-render work. Bring your pilot worksheet, example outputs and target formats to a[production scoping call](https://knowlify.com/book) . The decision is whether the private proposal addresses your production workload; the proposal can include end-to-end Meta campaign management or creative-only delivery, with media spend separate.


## FAQ


### How much does Arcads cost per month?


A current subscription dollar amount was not verifiable from the official public pages reviewed for this guide. Check the selected plan inside Arcads before paying, including the renewal price and billing term. Its documented credit allowances are 8,000 for Starter and 16,000 for Creator; those allowances are not prices or guaranteed finished-ad counts.


### Does Arcads offer a free trial?


Yes. The official FAQ describes 72 hours and 1,000 credits, with a card required and automatic conversion to Starter if you do not cancel in time. Prepare a small production task before signing up and check the deadline and amount due at renewal in your account.


### Do unused Arcads credits roll over?


Starter and Creator credits reset at renewal without rollover. The credit-plan documentation says Pro, Scale and Business retain unused credits while the subscription stays active. Check that rule alongside the chosen allowance and overage rate, especially if your production work arrives in uneven batches.


### Will Arcads refund a video I do not like?


Poor creative fit alone does not qualify for credit reimbursement under the published policy. Confirmed platform errors may qualify, with requests reviewed against the policy's conditions. Save the affected generation and contact support if you believe it failed technically; do not assume every rejected output will be free.


### Which Arcads alternative is best for a small team?


Start with the work the team can own. Evaluate Creatify for a product-URL workflow, HeyGen for avatar and language tasks, or a managed team when production capacity is the missing role. Use one approved script and a clear acceptance checklist for the shortlist. Our table describes buying fit, not measured superiority.


### Should I upgrade Arcads when a batch uses too many credits?


First examine why the batch consumed them. More capacity may help a reliable workflow, while late script changes or an unsuitable product treatment need a different fix. Record the actual generation actions and rejected attempts, then compare the next planned batch with the chosen plan’s allowance, reset rules and current price.
